The papersThe code

Housekeeper models, dug back up.

The authors fitted their models in R but never released the code. We rebuilt Models 1 and 2 from the paper's text as the R package hkselect and reran them on the paper's breast cancer data and on Vandesompele et al.'s data. Of 26 results we tried, 5 came back exact, 12 agree, 5 partly and 4 differ.

Ours, from an accurate Hessian, are within 0.002 of every printed bound.

R package hkselect and its tutorialAgreesR package hkselect: R CMD check OK; tests 23 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped; tutorial rendering equals the committed TUTORIAL.md (figures by name)

The main claims hold: MRPL19 is the best single gene and MRPL19, PUM1 and PSMC4 the chosen three-gene normaliser in breast cancer, and HPRT1, RPL13A and UBC the best small universal set. Of the results that do not match, Table 1's intervals differ in the third decimal as nlme's own do, two are slips in printed formulas, one is Table 2's last digit, and the rest follow from Model 2's SDs, which stay 2 to 5% below Table 3's for a reason we did not find.

p = 0.0014, from a likelihood ratio test the paper does not name.

All 50 squared biases within the resolution of the publisher's R graphics file.
Table 4
Every minimax gene set, once the bias of a set is the sum of its genes' biases, as the paper's own ACTB and TBP example also needs.

What stayed buried

  • Model 2's standard deviations: ours stay 2 to 5% below Table 3, and no variant fit we tried reaches it.
  • Table 2's six-gene value, 0.000004 on the other side of a rounding boundary.
  • How the paper computed its confidence intervals; nlme's own spread covers every printed bound.

The main claims hold: MRPL19 is the best single gene and MRPL19, PUM1 and PSMC4 the chosen three-gene normaliser in breast cancer, and HPRT1, RPL13A and UBC the best small universal set. Of the results that do not match, Table 1's intervals differ in the third decimal as nlme's own do, two are slips in printed formulas, one is Table 2's last digit, and the rest follow from Model 2's SDs, which stay 2 to 5% below Table 3's for a reason we did not find.
